fi-tropheus-moorii.title: Tropheus moorii
fi-tropheus-moorii.summary: Tropheus moorii is a cichlid endemic to Lake Tanganyika, found in shallow water around rocky shores and known in over 50 geographical morphs. Despite its popularity it is not a good species for the…
rows: groups (5-6 fish), the fish do not settle easily and may fight to the death.
It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach, nori etc.
notes: Many aquarists keep Tropheus in bare setups to reduce territorial behaviour but they can also be maintained in decorated aquaria.
If you wish to decorate the tank, use piles of rockwork to form many cave-like structures and hiding places, interspersed with open areas for swimming.

fi-cyphotilapia-frontosa.title: Frontosa
fi-cyphotilapia-frontosa.summary: The humphead cichlid, Cyphotilapia frontosa, is a large cichlid endemic to the northern portion of Lake Tanganyika. Known in the hobby as 'frontosa' or 'front', it grows to 255 mm SL and is…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group

Omnivore. This species is a generalised predator feeding on smaller fishes, macro -invertebrates, and molluscs , plus some algae and organic detritus which is presumably ingested when the fish are browsing the…
Endemic to the northern portion of Lake Tanganyika where it is distributed between Cape Tembwe on the western coast and Bulu Point on the eastern coast.
notes: A well-structured aquarium comprising some sheltered areas with plenty of open space is considered ideal.
A natural set-up could consist of a sandy substrate plus some piles of water-worn rocks of various sizes, some of which can be arranged to form cave-like structures, and perhaps a few large boulders.

fi-neolamprologus-brichardi.title: Brichardi Cichlid
fi-neolamprologus-brichardi.summary: Neolamprologus brichardi is a small cichlid endemic to Lake Tanganyika, found mainly over rocky shores in the northern half of the lake. Known in the hobby as the Princess of Burundi, it lives in…
rows: In the lake it feeds mainly on plankton picked from open water above the rocks (Hori et al., 1983).
Endemic to Lake Tanganyika , where it's recorded from the shores of Burundi , Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo .
notes: Set the tank up like the rocky shore of Lake Tanganyika, with piles of rock arranged to form caves over much of the aquarium and a sandy substrate.

fi-neolamprologus-multifasciatus.title: Lamprologus Multifasciatus Cichlid
fi-neolamprologus-multifasciatus.summary: Neolamprologus multifasciatus is a shell-brooding cichlid endemic to Lake Tanganyika, and probably the smallest known cichlid species. It lives in fairly deep water around the shoreline, over soft…
rows: Omnivore. Live and frozen varieties should form the bulk of the diet, although dried foods are usually accepted.
notes: The aquarium should have large open areas of sandy substrate, to which should be added a good number of empty snail shells (see breeding section below).
More shells should be provided than there are individual fish.

fi-tropheus-duboisi.title: Tropheus Duboisi Cichlid
fi-tropheus-duboisi.summary: The white-spotted cichlid, Tropheus duboisi, is endemic to Lake Tanganyika, found in rocky areas in deeper water than its congeners. Young fish have white or light blue spots on a jet black body,…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
groups (5-6 fish), the fish do not settle easily and may fight to the death.
Herbivore / algae browser. It will accept most foods offered but vegetable matter in the form of spirulina flakes, blanched spinach, nori etc.
notes: Many aquarists keep Tropheus in bare setups to reduce territorial behaviour but they can also be maintained in decorated aquaria.
If you wish to decorate the tank, use piles of rockwork to form many cave-like structures and hiding places, interspersed with open areas for swimming.

fi-altolamprologus-calvus.title: Black Inkfin Altolamprol. Calvus Cichlid
fi-altolamprologus-calvus.summary: The calvus cichlid, Altolamprologus calvus, is a laterally compressed predatory cichlid endemic to the rocky shores and islands of Lake Tanganyika. Its shape lets it enter crevices in the rockwork to…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Pairs or small groups depending on setup
Omnivore. Most meaty live and frozen foods are readily accepted.
notes: This fish should be housed in a Lake Tanganyika biotope setup, with piles of rocks arranged to form caves filling much of the aquarium.
Dim lighting will encourage it to be seen more often.

fi-cyprichromis-leptosoma.title: Blackfin Cyprichromis Leptosoma Cichlid
fi-cyprichromis-leptosoma.summary: The sardine cichlid, Cyprichromis leptosoma, is a peaceful open-water cichlid endemic to Lake Tanganyika. In nature it congregates in shoals of several thousand, feeding on zooplankton, and it occurs…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Most foods are accepted, but live and frozen varieties should form the bulk of the diet.
notes: As it's an open water species and will generally be found in the upper levels of the tank, the amount of swimming space takes precedence over the choice of decor.
Most hobbyists like to keep it in a community with other species, so a deep tank with rock piles arranged fairly close to the substrate is probably best.

fi-julidochromis-transcriptus.title: Julidochromis Transcriptus Cichlid
fi-julidochromis-transcriptus.summary: The masked julie, Julidochromis transcriptus, is a small cichlid endemic to the rocky coastal zones of northwestern Lake Tanganyika. It is known from between Luhanga and Makabola in the Democratic…
rows: Endemic to northwestern Lake Tanganyika , between Luhanga and Makabola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo , with type locality given simply as the 'extreme north' of the lake.

fi-lamprologus-ocellatus.title: Ocellated Lamprologus
fi-lamprologus-ocellatus.summary: The ocellated shell-dweller, Lamprologus ocellatus, is a small shell-brooding cichlid endemic to Lake Tanganyika. It buries its shell until only the entrance shows and defends it vigorously,…
rows: Omnivore. Live and frozen varieties should form the bulk of the diet, although dried foods are usually accepted.
notes: The setup should have open areas of sandy substrate to which should be added a good number of empty snail shells (see breeding section below).
More shells should be provided than there are individual fish.
